sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Sector breadth is extremely narrow with only Technology posting an all-green profile, while Industrials mount a short-term advance and Healthcare shows early signs of fading.

Market leadership remains heavily concentrated at the top. Technology stands alone with comprehensive strength across all timeframes, supported by a category-topping 0.950 momentum score, while Energy maintains the number one YTD rank with a 0.817 momentum reading. Industrials are the primary beneficiary of recent rotation, advancing two spots over the last five sessions into rank 3.

Conversely, breadth is pressured as 10 of 11 sectors fail to maintain positive returns across all measured horizons. Laggards are anchored by Utilities (0.217 momentum) and Consumer Cyclical (rank 11, 0.267 momentum). Meanwhile, recent slippage in Basic Materials and Healthcare highlights a loss of short-term stability among mid-tier groups.

## Strength
- Technology is the sole sector (1 of 11) exhibiting all-green breadth across week, month, quarter, half-year, and YTD windows, leading all groups with a 0.950 momentum score (YTD rank 2).
- Technology also demonstrates sustained strength, holding a top-3 ranking across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
- Energy holds the top spot overall with a YTD rank of 1 and robust momentum of 0.817.

## Movers & Momentum
- Industrials served as the top gainer over the past five sessions, climbing 2 spots to reach rank 3 with a 0.600 momentum score.
- Basic Materials dropped 1 spot over 5 sessions to rank 4, carrying a weak momentum score of 0.350.
- Momentum remains most depressed in Utilities (0.217 momentum, YTD rank 10), Real Estate (0.233 momentum, YTD rank 8), and Consumer Cyclical (0.267 momentum, YTD rank 11).

## Divergences
- Healthcare exhibits a fading profile: despite holding solid overall momentum of 0.683 (YTD rank 5), its rank declined by 1 spot over the last 5 sessions.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Leadership remains exceptionally narrow with only 10 of 144 groups all-green, anchored by dominant hardware tech and energy, while deep rotations hit materials and consumer-facing groups.

Overall market strength continues to be concentrated in technology hardware, industrial tech, and refining. Groups such as Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.988) and Computer Hardware (momentum 0.967) show sustained, multi-timeframe outperformance. Meanwhile, defensive and materials plays like Agricultural Inputs collapsed by 104 spots, marking severe deterioration at the bottom.

Rotational inflows are lifting beaten-down retail, real estate, and healthcare distribution names, though many remain in the lower half of overall rankings. Conversely, high-momentum cyclical groups including Copper and Steel are beginning to show early fatigue as their short-term ranks slip.

## Strength
- **Narrow leadership:** Only 10 of 144 industry groups maintain an all-green profile across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD windows.
- **Hardware and Energy dominance:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.988, rank 2 YTD), Electronics & Computer Distribution (momentum 0.974, rank 3 YTD), and Computer Hardware (momentum 0.967, rank 1 YTD) anchor the top tier.
- **Sustained momentum:** Semiconductors (momentum 0.939), Marine Shipping (momentum 0.939), Communication Equipment (0.91), Scientific & Technical Instruments (0.88), and Software - Infrastructure (0.83) all remain sustained top-36 performers across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Sharpest rank improvements:** Luxury Goods (+16 to rank 101, momentum 0.50), Medical Distribution (+16 to rank 57, momentum 0.73), and Real Estate - Diversified (+16 to rank 74, momentum 0.71) led the 5-session gains.
- **Consumer and building bid:** Building Products & Equipment gained 12 spots (rank 55, momentum 0.61), while Department Stores climbed 10 spots to rank 66 with a strong 0.80 momentum score.
- **Severe breakdowns:** Agricultural Inputs cratered 104 spots over 5 sessions to rank 138, holding the market's lowest momentum score at 0.015.
- **Persistent laggards:** Gambling (momentum 0.033, rank 143 YTD) and Advertising Agencies (momentum 0.049, rank 144 YTD) remain anchored at the bottom of the rankings.

## Divergences
- **Fading high-momentum cyclicals:** Early-warning rank declines have emerged in Diagnostics & Research (rank -5, momentum 0.76), Steel (rank -4, momentum 0.68), and Copper (rank -2, momentum 0.77).
- **Financial fatigue:** Banks - Diversified (momentum 0.60) and Insurance - Life (momentum 0.60) both slipped 2 rank spots over the past 5 sessions.
- **Emerging low-momentum rebounds:** Rank jumps accompanied by sub-0.50 momentum indicate early turnaround attempts in Apparel Manufacturing (+13 spots, momentum 0.47), Leisure (+8 spots, momentum 0.40), Travel Services (+7 spots, momentum 0.40), and Utilities - Regulated Electric (+7 spots, momentum 0.37).
